cache-aside.why: Check the cache, fall back to the source of truth on a miss, populate the cache, then answer.

stampede.why: Coalescing the misses (a lock or request collapsing) or early refresh with jitter prevents the thundering herd.

write-back-risk.why: Write-back acknowledges writes before they reach durable storage. It's fast and can lose data on failure.

why-queue.why: Decoupling lets each side scale and fail independently; the queue buffers bursts.

duplicates.why: At-least-once means duplicates happen (e.g. after a timeout). Dedupe keys or idempotent writes make them harmless.

dead-letter.why: After a few failed attempts a message moves aside for investigation instead of being retried forever.

ttl-staleness.why: TTLs bound staleness rather than prevent it. Invalidate on write when freshness matters.
